question: When checking the air gauge during a pre-trip inspection, the air compressor should build air pressure to governor cut-out at approximately what psi range (unless the manufacturer specifies otherwise)?
explanation: The manual states the air compressor should build air pressure to governor cut-out at approximately 120-140 psi or as specified by the manufacturer.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-1

question: As part of checking emergency equipment, a driver must confirm the vehicle carries three red reflective triangles and which of the following?
choice_a: 6 fusees or 3 liquid burning flares
choice_b: 2 spare tires
choice_c: A second fire extinguisher
choice_d: 4 wheel chocks
explanation: The manual specifies checking for three red reflective triangles and 6 fusees or 3 liquid burning flares as part of the emergency equipment check.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-1

question: During the windshield check, what should a driver look for?
choice_a: That the windshield is clean with no illegal stickers, obstructions, or damage to the glass
choice_b: That the windshield has a valid inspection sticker
choice_c: That the windshield tint meets state minimums
choice_d: That the windshield wiper fluid reservoir is full
explanation: The manual states the windshield should be clean with no illegal stickers, no obstructions, or damage to the glass.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-1

question: When checking lights and reflectors for correct color, clearance lights should be which colors?
choice_a: Amber on rear, red elsewhere
choice_b: Red on rear, amber elsewhere
choice_c: White on rear, red elsewhere
choice_d: All amber
explanation: The manual specifies clearance lights should be red on the rear and amber elsewhere as part of verifying correct light and reflector color.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-1

question: How is the parking brake checked to confirm it will hold the vehicle?
choice_a: By checking that the dash warning light for the parking brake is off
choice_b: By gently trying to pull the vehicle forward with the parking brake engaged
choice_c: By listening for air leaks at the brake chambers
choice_d: By measuring pushrod travel with the brakes released
explanation: With air pressure built to governor cutout and the parking brake engaged, the manual directs checking that the parking brake will hold the vehicle by gently trying to pull forward with the parking brake on.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-1

question: During the hydraulic brake check, after pumping the brake pedal three times and holding it down, what should happen for five seconds?
choice_a: The brake pedal should slowly sink to the floor
choice_b: The brake pedal should not move (depress) during the five seconds
choice_c: The warning buzzer should sound continuously
choice_d: The parking brake should automatically release
explanation: The manual instructs pumping the brake pedal three times, then holding it down for five seconds, during which the brake pedal should not move (depress).
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-2

question: During the air brake check, after building air pressure to governor cutoff and holding the foot brake for one minute, how much can air pressure drop without failing the check on a single vehicle versus a combination vehicle?
choice_a: No more than 3 psi for a single vehicle, no more than 4 psi for a combination vehicle
choice_b: No more than 5 psi for a single vehicle, no more than 10 psi for a combination vehicle
choice_c: No more than 4 psi for a single vehicle, no more than 3 psi for a combination vehicle
choice_d: No more than 2 psi for either vehicle type
explanation: The manual states the air pressure should not drop more than three pounds in one minute for a single vehicle or four pounds in one minute for a combination vehicle.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-2

question: While fanning off air pressure during the air brake check, the low air warning devices (buzzer, light, or flag) should activate before the air pressure drops below what level (unless the manufacturer specifies otherwise)?
choice_a: 20 psi
choice_b: 45 psi
choice_c: 55 psi
choice_d: 70 psi
explanation: The manual states low air warning devices should activate before air pressure drops below 55 psi or the level specified by the manufacturer.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-2

question: On a tractor-trailer combination vehicle, at what air pressure range should the tractor protection valve and parking brake valve close (pop out) as air pressure continues to be fanned off?
choice_a: 0-10 psi
explanation: The manual states that at a range between 20-45 psi (or the level specified by the manufacturer), the tractor protection valve and parking brake valve should close (pop out) on a tractor-trailer combination.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-2

question: How is the service brake check performed to determine the brakes are working correctly?
choice_a: Pull forward at 5 mph, apply the service brake, and check that the vehicle does not pull to either side and stops
choice_b: Back the vehicle 10 feet while applying the brake
choice_c: Apply the brake while stationary and check the air gauge for a drop
choice_d: Drive at highway speed and perform a hard stop
explanation: The manual directs pulling forward at 5 mph, applying the service brake, and checking that the vehicle does not pull to either side and that it stops when the brake is applied.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-2

question: When inspecting the steering box and hoses, what should a driver check for in addition to secure mounting and missing nuts or bolts?
choice_a: Power steering fluid leaks or damage to power steering hoses
choice_b: Correct tire pressure on the steering axle
choice_c: Proper alignment of the headlights
choice_d: Wear on the brake linings
explanation: The manual states to check for power steering fluid leaks or damage to power steering hoses as part of the steering box/hoses inspection.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-2

question: When inspecting suspension springs, what type of damage should a driver look for in leaf springs specifically?
choice_a: Missing, shifted, cracked, or broken leaf springs
choice_b: Excessive rust only
choice_c: Incorrect paint color
choice_d: Loose wheel bearings
explanation: The manual instructs looking for missing, shifted, cracked, or broken leaf springs during the suspension inspection.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-2

question: For a manual slack adjustor, how far should the brake pushrod move (with the brakes released) when pulled by hand before it indicates a problem?
choice_a: It should not move at all
choice_b: It should not move more than one inch
choice_c: It should not move more than six inches
choice_d: It should move freely with no resistance
explanation: The manual states that for manual slack adjustors, the brake pushrod should not move more than one inch (with the brakes released) when pulled by hand.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-2

question: What is the minimum tread depth required on steering axle tires compared to all other tires?
choice_a: 2/32 on steering axle tires, 4/32 on all other tires
choice_b: 4/32 on steering axle tires, 2/32 on all other tires
choice_c: 6/32 on steering axle tires, 4/32 on all other tires
choice_d: The same 4/32 minimum applies to all tires
explanation: The manual specifies a minimum tread depth of 4/32 on steering axle tires and 2/32 on all other tires.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-3

question: According to the manual, how must a driver check tire inflation to receive credit on the inspection?
choice_a: By using a tire gauge, not by kicking the tires or using a mallet
choice_b: By kicking each tire firmly
choice_c: By using a mallet to strike the sidewall
choice_d: By visually estimating sidewall bulge
explanation: The manual states tire inflation must be checked using a tire gauge, and that a driver will not get credit for simply kicking the tires or using a mallet to check inflation.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-3

question: What repair is not permitted on a rim when inspecting the wheels?
choice_a: Rims cannot have welding repairs
choice_b: Rims cannot have any rust
choice_c: Rims cannot be repainted
choice_d: Rims cannot be replaced with a different brand
explanation: The manual states rims cannot have welding repairs, and that rims should be checked for rust trails that may indicate the rim is loose on the wheel.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-3

question: For a vehicle equipped with emissions after-treatment equipment, what should a driver check regarding the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) tank?
choice_a: That the DEF tank level is adequate, meaning more than 1/8th tank
choice_b: That the DEF tank is completely full
choice_c: That the DEF tank cap is removed for inspection
choice_d: That the DEF tank is drained before inspection
explanation: The manual states that for vehicles with emissions after-treatment equipment, the driver checks the DEF tank to ensure the level of diesel exhaust fluid is adequate (more than 1/8th tank) and that the DEF indicator on the dash is working properly.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-4

question: When inspecting the fifth wheel kingpin, apron, and gap on a tractor-trailer, what must a driver explain and check?
choice_a: That locking jaws hold the kingpin in place, the kingpin is not bent or damaged, and the trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate with no gap
choice_b: That the kingpin is painted a reflective color
choice_c: That the fifth wheel has been recently greased within the last 24 hours
choice_d: That the apron is removed entirely for inspection
explanation: The manual directs the driver to explain that locking jaws hold the kingpin in place and that the kingpin is not bent or damaged, that the visible part of the apron is not bent, cracked, or broken, and that the trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate (no gap).
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-4

question: In addition to the standard emergency equipment (fuses, triangles, flares, and fire extinguisher), what additional emergency equipment must school bus drivers inspect?
choice_a: An emergency kit and a body fluid cleanup kit
choice_b: A second fire extinguisher and a tow chain
choice_c: A spare tire and jack
choice_d: A GPS unit and two-way radio
explanation: The manual states that school bus drivers must also inspect an Emergency Kit and a Body Fluid Cleanup Kit in addition to the standard emergency equipment.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-5

question: How many different equivalent versions of the vehicle inspection test does a Class A CDL applicant need to be prepared to perform, not knowing in advance which one will be given?
choice_a: Two
choice_b: Three
choice_c: Four
choice_d: Five
explanation: The manual states that a Class A CDL applicant will be required to perform one of four equivalent versions of the vehicle inspection test, not knowing which one until just before testing begins.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-9
